text:
# Hierarchical and Local Scene Decomposition

Also called: Local Neural Fields, Incremental Implicit Scene Representation, Adaptive Voronoi NeRFs

## Overview
Hierarchical and Local Scene Decomposition addresses the memory constraints and convergence issues of global [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) representations when applied to large-scale or long-sequence [scenes by partitioning](#8353-large-scene-reconstruction-via-chunking.md) the scene into multiple local radiance fields [S1]. Unlike global implicit representations that evaluate a single large MLP for every sample, these methods use a structured collection of local fields (e.g., [Nerflets](#8263-nerflets.md) or sliding-window local radiance fields) to enable efficient, structure-aware scene [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md) and interactive editing [S1, 20286-nerf-with-local-neural-fields-nerflets.md].

## Shared principles
The family shares the mechanism of decomposing a 3D scene into a set of $N$ local representations rather than a single global function. Each local representation $i$ maintains its own spatial parameters (position, orientation, extent) and a local neural network or feature grid.

1.  **Local [Coordinate Transformation](#22961-coordinate-transformations.md):** For a query point $x$, it is transformed into the local coordinate frame of each contributing local field $i$ using the field's center $\mu_i$, [rotation](#19376-rotation.md) $\theta_i$, and scale/radii $r_i$.
2.  **Influence Weighting:** Each local field contributes to the final density and color based on an influence weight $w_{k,i}$, which typically falls off with distance from the field's center, often modeled by a Radial Basis Function (RBF) [S1, 20286-nerf-with-local-neural-fields-nerflets.md].
3.  **Aggregation:** The effective density $\sigma_k$ and color $c_k$ at a sample point are computed as weighted sums of the outputs from all nearby local fields:
    $$ \sigma_k = \sum_{i} w_{k,i} \sigma_{k,i} $$
    $$ c_k = \frac{\sum_{i} w_{k,i} \sigma_{k,i} c_{k,i}}{\sum_{i} w_{k,i} \sigma_{k,i}} $$
    [20286-nerf-with-local-neural-fields-nerflets.md]
4.  **Volume Rendering:** Standard volume rendering integration is performed using the aggregated density and color values [S1, 20286-nerf-with-local-neural-fields-nerflets.md].

## Subtopics

### [NeRF with Local Neural Fields (Nerflets)](20286-nerf-with-local-neural-fields-nerflets.md)
Nerflets represent a scene as an irregular collection of local [neural radiance fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md), where each "nerflet" maintains its own pose and influence region. It differs from global NeRF by evaluating only small MLPs of nearby nerflets, enabling efficient structure-aware reconstruction and 2D-supervised semantic/instance editing [20286-nerf-with-local-neural-fields-nerflets.md].

### [Incremental Implicit Scene Representation](21737-incremental-implicit-scene-representation.md)
This method reconstructs large-scale scenes by dynamically allocating local radiance fields as the camera moves, using a sliding window of frames. It differs from global NeRF by using [Vector-Matrix decomposition](#9759-tensorf-vector-matrix-decomposition.md) for feature grids, reducing space complexity from cubic $O(n^3)$ to square $O(n)$ and solving memory constraints for long sequences [21737-incremental-implicit-scene-representation.md].

### Adaptive Voronoi NeRFs
A technique presented by Elsner et al. that enhances efficiency by employing Voronoi diagrams to partition the scene into cells. These cells are subsequently subdivided to effectively capture and represent intricate details, leading to improved performance and accuracy [S1].

## Background
The concept of decomposing scenes into local fields emerged to address the scalability limits of global NeRFs. Elsner et al. introduced Adaptive Voronoi NeRFs to improve efficiency through spatial partitioning [S1]. Concurrently, methods like Nerflets and [Incremental Implicit Scene Representation](#21737-incremental-implicit-scene-representation.md) were developed to handle large-scale environments and long sequences by avoiding the optimization of a single monolithic network, thereby reducing memory usage and improving convergence [20286-nerf-with-local-neural-fields-nerflets.md, 21737-incremental-implicit-scene-representation.md].

## Sources
